answer: An agent economy can require every vertex to lock a scarce pearl-token deposit before it may submit work, then slash that deposit when independent audits catch fabricated identities coordinating to claim rewards. The audit samples outputs and checks shared funding and behavior, so minting many names does not multiply trustworthy votes. A sybil attacker must acquire and tie up real capital for each identity, while risking forfeiture; spreading attacks across a longer horizon raises that cost rather than making identities free.
